abstract: This study presents a machine learning based simulation for predicting air pollution impact on climate temperature fluctuations and human health. Using synthetic data generated through statistical modeling, seven types of air pollution sources and seven key pollutants were simulated. Machine learning models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, Neural Networks, and others, were applied to evaluate the correlation between pollution levels, air quality index (AQI), and predicted health impacts. Results indicate strong predictive capabilities of ensemble models for environmental monitoring, demonstrating accuracy levels between 70 to 99%. This approach provides a scalable framework for forecasting pollution-driven health risks where measured data are unavailable.
